# SE-EDU naming standard

Follow the CS2103/T [code-quality naming guidelines](https://nus-cs2103-ay2627-s1.github.io/website/schedule/week4/topics.html#w4-6-code-quality-naming)
for all Java production code in this repository. Apply these rules together with the project's
Java coding standard and other code-quality rules.

## Naming rules

- Use nouns or noun phrases for classes and variables, and verbs or verb phrases for methods.
- Distinguish single values from collections clearly; use plural names for collections.
- Use correctly spelled, standard English. Avoid texting-style spelling, foreign-language words,
  slang, private references, and references that depend on a temporary cultural context.
- Choose names that explain each entity accurately and with enough detail to reveal its purpose.
  Arrange words in a natural, meaningful order.
- Do not distinguish names only by numbers or letter case. Name the role or difference instead,
  such as `originalValue` and `finalValue` rather than `value1` and `value2`.
- Prefer concise names, but do not sacrifice clarity merely to make a name shorter.
- Use abbreviations and acronyms only when they remain understandable. Apply them consistently and
  explain unfamiliar ones in an obvious project-level location.
- Give related concepts consistently structured names. Give unrelated concepts visibly different
  names even when their types or implementations are similar.
- Avoid ambiguous, misleading, easily confused, or hard-to-pronounce names, including names whose
  characters or sounds can be mistaken for one another.
